section_summary: The section begins with the final statistical tables of a study of Japanese public finance, covering revenue, expenditure, war spending, government bond issues, and the 1940–41 budget. Later documents address Japanese bonds imported into the Philippines, proposed American investment in Mitsubishi, Japanese efforts to obtain foreign credit, and a proposed loan for shipping purchases. Three cross-reference sheets point to related records on flour transactions and credit in China.

subfiles.title: Tables of Japanese revenue, expenditure, war spending, bond issues, and budget estimates
subfiles.about: Statistical tables trace Japanese public finances through the 1940–41 budget.
subfiles.summary: The concluding tables give ordinary and extraordinary revenue and expenditure, the temporary war expenditure special account, government bond issues, and comparative 1939–40 and 1940–41 budget estimates. They show rising military spending, debt, and reliance on loans, with citations to Japanese financial publications and the Mitsubishi Monthly Circular.

subfiles.title: Telegram concerning eight Japanese government bonds in Iloilo
subfiles.about: The Philippine authorities seek advice on returning eight imported Japanese government bonds to their sender.
subfiles.summary: Sayre asks for Securities and Exchange Commission advice on returning bonds whose importation may have violated the Securities Act of 1933.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting an opinion on return of Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: The Department requests an opinion on whether the Securities Act permits the bonds' return.
subfiles.summary: The Department distinguishes the federal securities question from any action under the Philippine Revised Administrative Code, which it considers a Commonwealth matter.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on proposed Tidewater subscription to Mitsubishi stock
subfiles.about: Officials consider Tidewater Associated Oil Company's proposed purchase of Mitsubishi shares.
subfiles.summary: The proposed ¥275,000 purchase would be funded from dividends owed by a Japanese oil subsidiary. The memorandum recommends telling Tumulty that the Department hopes Tidewater will decline.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Joseph Tumulty on Japanese company stock
subfiles.about: Tumulty asks whether the Department objects to Tidewater buying Mitsubishi stock.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton requests details before giving a definite view. He describes the Department's concerns about assistance to Japan's venture in China and Japan's credit and exchange restrictions.

subfiles.title: Further conversation with Joseph Tumulty on Mitsubishi stock
subfiles.about: Tumulty corrects the proposed subscription amount and supplies details of Mitsubishi's new issue.
subfiles.summary: Tidewater proposes to buy 2,500 shares worth ¥275,000, using dividends from its jointly owned Japanese oil subsidiary rather than remitting new funds. Tumulty explains Mitsubishi's capitalization plans, mentions Westinghouse's possible subscription, and seeks the Department's view.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding stock purchase memoranda to the ambassador
subfiles.about: The Department forwards memoranda about proposed American purchases of Japanese company stock.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the July 12 and July 15 conversation memoranda for the ambassador's information.

subfiles.title: Commission opinion on return of Japanese government bonds
subfiles.about: The Securities and Exchange Commission addresses whether the eight bonds may be returned.
subfiles.summary: Frank reports counsel's opinion that returning the bonds would not violate the Securities Act of 1933.

subfiles.title: Telegram conveying bond return opinion to Manila
subfiles.about: The Department relays the Commission's opinion to the Philippine authorities.
subfiles.summary: Returning the bonds does not violate the Securities Act; the Commonwealth must decide the question under Philippine law.

subfiles.title: Conversation reporting Tidewater's decision
subfiles.about: Tumulty reports Tidewater's decision on the Mitsubishi stock offer.
subfiles.summary: In light of the Department's views, Tidewater decided against subscribing.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding the later Tumulty conversation
subfiles.about: The Department sends the ambassador a later memorandum concerning the proposed stock purchase.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the conversation memorandum for the ambassador's confidential information.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on “Wartime Public Finance of Japan”
subfiles.about: An official recommends portions of a Chinese Council for Economic Research bulletin.
subfiles.summary: Directs readers to its summary and wartime expenditure tables, noting overlap with an existing State Department study.

subfiles.title: Japanese efforts to make purchases abroad on credit
subfiles.from: H. H. Smith Hutton, Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The report describes Japanese attempts to obtain foreign credit for essential imports.
subfiles.summary: Japan had obtained credit for some wheat, rice, and cotton purchases. Japanese oil companies reportedly made false claims that American competitors had extended credit, but the contemplated oil credits were stopped.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on credit to Japanese interests in China
subfiles.about: Points to a conversation about credit and a wheat flour shipment to Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: References a Jones–Macgregor memorandum filed at 893.51/7113.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on guarantees for a flour transaction
subfiles.about: Points to a conversation about proposed credit guarantees for a flour purchase.
subfiles.summary: References an Allman memorandum filed at 893.51/7117.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on a flour purchase for distribution in China
subfiles.about: Points to a conversation with a Japanese Embassy counselor about flour purchase negotiations.
subfiles.summary: References a Hamilton memorandum filed at 893.51/7122.

subfiles.title: Shanghai telegram on proposed shipping loan, section one
subfiles.about: A Shanghai corporation proposes a dollar loan to Japanese buyers of shipping tonnage.
subfiles.summary: The China Foreign Trade Corporation agreed to lend up to $2 million, secured through the Yokohama Specie Bank. The stated purpose was to finance ship purchases, with repayment deferred partly because of Japanese foreign exchange procedures.

subfiles.title: Shanghai telegram on proposed shipping loan, section two
subfiles.about: Further details describe the loan's terms and uncertainty about its completion.
subfiles.summary: Vice chairman Fritz Schick describes the transaction as secured lending at a favorable rate. The local bank manager doubts the Yokohama Specie Bank will support it; the vessels may be formerly Chinese-owned coastal ships at Shanghai.
